_comment: Raptor's egg library (library/README.md). Written for Raptor.
name: TriliumNext Notes
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: TriliumNext Notes is a self-hosted app for building a large personal knowledge base of hierarchical notes. Open the server's address to set the password, or connect Trilium desktop to sync.
startup: export TRILIUM_DATA_DIR=/home/container/data TRILIUM_NETWORK_HOST=0.0.0.0 TRILIUM_NETWORK_PORT={{SERVER_PORT}}; unset TRILIUM_PORT; cd trilium && exec ./node/bin/node main.mjs

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# TriliumNext Notes: downloads the Trilium server (with its own Node.js)
# from its GitHub releases, checked against GitHub's SHA-256, into
# trilium/. Your notes (data/: the database, backups, config.ini) are
# never touched; trilium/ is only replaced once the new one is unpacked.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server
work=/mnt/server/.raptor-build
rm -rf "$work" && mkdir -p "$work"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }

case "$(uname -m)" in
    x86_64) arch=x64 ;;
    aarch64) arch=arm64 ;;
    *) fail "Trilium has no build for this CPU ($(uname -m))." ;;
esac

want="${VERSION:-latest}"
[ "$want" = latest ] || want="v${want#v}"
tag=$(gh-release tag TriliumNext/Trilium "$want") || fail "Set Version to latest, or to a release such as 0.107.0, then reinstall."

if [ -x trilium/node/bin/node ] && [ "$(cat .trilium-version 2>/dev/null)" = "$tag" ]; then
    echo "Trilium $tag is already installed."
else
    echo "Downloading Trilium $tag"
    gh-release download TriliumNext/Trilium "$tag" "TriliumNotes-Server-$tag-linux-$arch.tar.xz" "$work/trilium.tar.xz"
    mkdir "$work/new"
    tar -xJf "$work/trilium.tar.xz" -C "$work/new" --strip-components=1
    [ -x "$work/new/node/bin/node" ] && [ -f "$work/new/main.mjs" ] || fail "The download isn't a Trilium server. Reinstall to try again."
    # Trilium's web interface asks GitHub for new releases by default: new
    # notes databases start with that off (turn it on in Options, About).
    if grep -lq '{name:"checkForUpdates",value:"true"' "$work"/new/chunks/*.mjs 2>/dev/null; then
        sed -i 's/{name:"checkForUpdates",value:"true"/{name:"checkForUpdates",value:"false"/' "$work"/new/chunks/*.mjs
    fi
    rm -rf trilium.old
    [ ! -d trilium ] || mv trilium trilium.old
    mv "$work/new" trilium
    rm -rf trilium.old
    echo "$tag" > .trilium-version
fi
mkdir -p data
echo "Installed Trilium $tag."

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The Trilium version to install, such as 0.107.0, or latest. Reinstall to change it.
